causalModel.founding: A mixed village at the road's water point: an Imperial well on the south bench, an Argonian landing on the north bank across the ford. The landing is older than the station.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: A perennial spring beside a boat channel, where the road fords the water.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: Two communities share it because neither can hold the other's half.
causalModel.pressures: The well is Imperial-built and failing. The landing will not help to repair it in stone.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: Would become one community or two villages within a generation.

districts.notes: The Imperial half on the south bench.

why.what: The well-station: the station house, the stable, the lean-to and the well.
why.whyHere: The Imperial half keeps the well and the road trade.
why.whyNeighbours: It faces the landing across the ford, along the road.
why.playerPurpose: A bed, food for the road, a stable for a horse and water from the well.
why.microGeography: A narrow bench between the channel and the hillside, raised on stone pads.

districts.notes: The Argonian half on the north strip; no Hist (see siting).

why.what: The landing hamlet: three mud huts round an open common, the fish racks and the boats pulled up on the bank.
why.whyHere: The landing is older than the station; its polers came up from the mud-hut country and built as they do at home, on the dry point by the channel.
why.whyNeighbours: It faces the well-station across the ford. It keeps no Hist: its people's tree stands at Fenmarch Village (place.imperial-fringe.fenmarch-village, 1.7 km). They go home for the hatching.
why.playerPurpose: The ford ferry for carts and beasts; the landing's side of LF83.
why.microGeography: The dry strip on the ford's north bank, huts on mud pads raised a little above the channel.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its long wall runs with the road and its door turns north-east onto the path from the street.

playerPurpose.note: Lodging upstairs and the well-keeper's provisions counter at the door (LF83 counter 1).

why.what: The station house: the well-keeper's home, with beds for travellers upstairs and the provisions counter at the door.
why.whyHere: A road station keeps a house where travellers sleep and buy food; this one belongs to the well-keeper.
why.whySpot: The widest dry ground on the south bench, beside the well junction and square to the road.
why.whyNeighbours: It stands behind the well and the lean-to, so the fire, the well and the door are seen together from the street.
why.playerPurpose: A bed for the night and food for the road; the first of the two counters in LF83.
why.microGeography: The bench rises to the south; the house stands on a stone pad that takes up the fall.

parcels.orientationWhy: The windlass turns across the road so the bucket is drawn from the street side.

why.what: The Imperial well, its head cracked, at the junction of the street and the station path.
why.whyHere: The well is the reason for the place. It is the road's water point.
why.whySpot: On the raised bench east of the station house, above the road junction and the tarn.
why.whyNeighbours: The station house, the handcart and the lantern post stand round it.
why.playerPurpose: Water, a landmark from the south road and the cracked well of LF83.
why.microGeography: A levelled step on the bench, two metres above the tarn and 1.5 m above the road.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs along the road frontage, south of the lean-to.

why.what: A dry-stone wall along the station's road frontage.
why.whyHere: Imperial yards are walled on the road side.
why.whySpot: South of the lean-to along the road verge, leaving the well junction open.
why.whyNeighbours: It closes the yard between the station house and the road.
why.playerPurpose: It marks the station's yard from the road.
why.microGeography: It follows the verge where the road climbs to the south-east.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs along the station house's long back wall, square to the pad.

why.what: A dry-stone retaining wall along the back of the station house's pad.
why.whyHere: The house stands on a raised stone pad; the wall holds the pad's edge where the bench falls away.
why.whySpot: Along the pad's long back edge, two paces out from the house wall.
why.whyNeighbours: It closes the pad behind the house; the end walls meet it at the corners.
why.playerPurpose: It shows why the house stands level on a sloping bench.
why.microGeography: The bench falls below this edge, so the wall stands tallest here.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs across the pad's north-east end, square to the house.

why.what: A dry-stone retaining wall across the north-east end of the station house's pad.
why.whyHere: This end of the pad stands highest over the slope down to the stable, so its edge needs holding.
why.whySpot: Across the pad's north-east end, above the stable yard.
why.whyNeighbours: It joins the back wall at the corner and stops short of the yard wall on the road side.
why.playerPurpose: It closes the pad on the stable side, so the yard ends at a wall.
why.microGeography: The ground drops toward the stable below this end.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs across the pad's south-west end, square to the house.

why.what: A dry-stone retaining wall across the south-west end of the station house's pad.
why.whyHere: The bench dips at the house's landing end. The wall keeps the pad from slumping there.
why.whySpot: Across the pad's end away from the stable, behind the woodpile and the hen's nest.
why.whyNeighbours: It joins the back wall at one corner and the road-side yard wall at the other.
why.playerPurpose: It closes the pad on the landing side, behind the woodpile.
why.microGeography: The bench slopes away toward the landing below this end.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs across the stable's south end, square to the pad.

why.what: A dry-stone retaining wall along the south side of the stable's pad.
why.whyHere: The stable's pad is cut into the ground at this end; the wall holds the bank back from the stalls.
why.whySpot: Along the pad's south edge, two paces out from the stable's end.
why.whyNeighbours: It meets the west wall at the pad's south-west corner.
why.playerPurpose: It keeps the bank off the stable's south end.
why.microGeography: The ground stands higher than the pad along most of this edge.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs across the stable's north end, square to the pad.

why.what: A dry-stone retaining wall along the north side of the stable's pad.
why.whyHere: The pad is cut into the rising ground at the stable's north end; the wall keeps the bank off it.
why.whySpot: Along the pad's north edge, facing the station house.
why.whyNeighbours: It stops short of the pad's north-west corner, leaving the gap where the stable path turns in to the stalls.
why.playerPurpose: It keeps the bank off the stable's north end.
why.microGeography: The bench rises above this edge toward the station house.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall runs along the open front of the stalls, square to the pad.

why.what: A dry-stone retaining wall along the west edge of the stable's pad, in front of the stalls.
why.whyHere: The pad is cut into the ground on its west side; the wall keeps the slope from slumping into the yard.
why.whySpot: Along the pad's west edge, a few paces out from the stalls.
why.whyNeighbours: It joins the north and south walls at the pad's corners.
why.playerPurpose: It closes the stable's pad on the side that faces the landing.
why.microGeography: The ground rises above this end toward the bench.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door turns south to the path down to the ford and the landing.

playerPurpose.note: The poler's home and the crossing fee (LF83 counter 2); the ferry is run from the landing below it.

why.what: The poler's hut, where the crossing fee is paid.
why.whyHere: The landing hamlet lives by the crossing; the poler lives beside it.
why.whySpot: The east end of the north strip, above the ford's north bank.
why.whyNeighbours: The fish racks and the landing lie between it and the water; the common is to the west.
why.playerPurpose: The ford ferry for carts and beasts; the second counter of LF83.
why.microGeography: Dry ground above the channel on a mud pad raised clear of the wet bank.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door turns north-east to the Blackwood Road, which bends round it.

playerPurpose.note: The landing family's home, where the player hears the landing's side of the argument over the well (LF83).

why.what: The family hut of the landing, where one household of the landing lives.
why.whyHere: The landing's families live on the dry point by the channel.
why.whySpot: West of the road on the inside of its bend, the driest ground on the north bank.
why.whyNeighbours: The road runs past its door; the landing and the poler's pod are across the road to the east.
why.playerPurpose: A home to enter and people to talk to about the well and the landing.
why.microGeography: Dry ground on a mud pad raised clear of the wet bank.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door faces east onto the store path, a few metres above the landing's dock where the catch comes ashore.

why.what: The landing's net and basket maker works in this pod, beside the stored catch.
why.whyHere: A landing needs its nets mended and its baskets woven close to the boats.
why.whySpot: North of the landing steps on the dry bank, clear of the road.
why.whyNeighbours: The landing steps run past its door; the poler's pod stands to the south-west.
why.playerPurpose: A workshop on the landing whose door the player can open.
why.microGeography: Dry bank a metre above the channel, its pad raised clear of the wet ground.

playerPurpose.note: The crafter's household, where the player hears how the landing lives off the catch and the crossing.

parcels.orientationWhy: The raft lies with its long side to the bank for boarding.

why.what: The ferry raft, moored in the channel east of the landing.
why.whyHere: Carts and beasts cross on it, so the hull stays afloat by the landing.
why.whySpot: The nearest water that floats it: at least a metre all round, east of the road.
why.whyNeighbours: The cleats on the bank hold it; the landing path runs to it.
why.playerPurpose: The ferry that carries carts, beasts and the player across the ford.
why.microGeography: Channel water at 35.24 m, more than a metre deep round the hull.

parcels.orientationWhy: The open stalls face west-south-west into the walled paddock, their backs to the road.

why.what: An open stable of four stalls where travellers' horses stand for the night.
why.whyHere: A road station keeps a stable for animals that cannot come inside.
why.whySpot: The levelled yard south-east of the station house, walled on three sides. Nowhere else near the road is level and wide enough for the stalls and a paddock.
why.whyNeighbours: Stone walls close the paddock in front of the stalls on three sides; the station house stands to the north-west.
why.playerPurpose: A stable where the player's horse is kept for the night.
why.microGeography: A levelled yard cut into the foot of the hillside.

parcels.orientationWhy: The two dock spans run from the dry bank straight out to the raft's berth.

why.what: The landing stage: two plank dock spans on piles from the bank out over the channel.
why.whyHere: The ferry raft needs a dry way out to water deep enough to float it.
why.whySpot: From the bank east of the poler's pod, the shortest way to a metre of water.
why.whyNeighbours: The raft lies at its end; the cleats and the canoe are at its foot.
why.playerPurpose: The way from the bank to the ferry raft.
why.microGeography: The deck stands a hand's breadth over the channel; its piles go down into the bed.

routes.why: The Blackwood Road between the well junction and the ford: the street both halves face.
From the street to the station house door.
The short worn step from the road to the well head.
From the well junction round the outside of the north yard wall, then in at the yard's west side to the open front of the stalls.
From the ford's north bank past the fish racks to the moored raft.
From the landing path on the ford's north bank up to the poler's pod house.
From the poler's path across the common to the family hut's door.
From the common west along the strip to the store hut.

approaches.sequence: Coming down the road from the south-east, the station house roof and its smoke show first, then the well at the junction and the lean-to by the fire; the ford and the huts beyond open up at the junction.
approaches.wayfinding: The road runs past the yard wall to the well junction; the station house path leaves the street there.

approaches.sequence: Coming from the north-west, the hut domes and the landing lanterns show first; the road passes between the huts to the ford. The well roof shows across the water.
approaches.wayfinding: Follow the road through the landing to the ford; the poler's hut stands on the bank above it.

networkTerminals.why: The Blackwood Road arrives from Gideon along the bench to the south-east.
The road leaves the ford's north bank toward Blackwood through the landing.

combatSpaces.why: The street between the well and the ford, where a road fight at the station happens.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: type recipe road-station-village (a keeper and travellers); record occupants D1 family (few), D2 travellers (few); roster npcs.json well-keeper and poler
scaleGrounding.why: Two named keepers and one landing family live here; travellers come and go. Six buildings stand, three in the well-station and three in the landing; the dry ground holds no seventh. Beside them stand the well, the lean-to, the ferry raft and the dry-stone walls that hold the two station pads.

candidates.why: The only dry ground on both banks of the ford: the south bench for the well-station and the north strip for the landing.
The flat pad east of the road beside the channel.
candidates.rejectedBecause: One flat pad east of the road; the rest of the east side is open water at 35.24 m, with no room for either half.

exceptions.reason: No third linked Argonian shell with a usable cell: mudhut02 (KeebaHouseElder) was tried in the residual round. Its door stands 4.7 m above the ground at every scanned pose with no stair or walkway in the kit to reach it, so the store keeps its King of the Murkmire pod.
